-- pattern-utils.hs - utilities to use in TidalCycles

-- A function that alternates between two patterns every n cycles:
alternate :: Int -> a -> a -> [a]
alternate n a b = concat (replicate n [a, b])
-- alternate 2 "bd" "sn" = ["bd","bd","sn","sn","bd","bd","sn","sn"]

-- A function that interleavse two lists:
interleave :: [a] -> [a] -> [a]
interleave []     ys     = ys
interleave xs     []     = xs
interleave (x:xs) (y:ys) = x : y : interleave xs ys
-- interleave [1,2,3] [10,20,30] = [1,10,2,20,3,30]

-- Map a transformation over every nth element:
everyNth :: Int -> (a -> a) -> [a] -> [a]
everyNth n f xs = zipWith apply [0..] xs
  where apply i x = if i `mod` n == 0 then f x else x

-- Generate a Euclidean rhythm as a list of Booleans
-- euclidean k n: k beats distributed as evenly as possible over n steps
euclidean :: Int -> Int -> [Bool]
euclidean k n = go k (n - k) (replicate k [True]) (replicate (n-k) [False])
  where
    go 0 _  acc _       = concat acc
    go _ _  acc []      = concat acc
    go k' r' acc extras
        | k' <= r'  = go (min k' (length extras)) (r' - k') (zipWith (++) acc extras) (drop k' extras)
        | otherwise = go (r' `mod` k') (k' - r') acc extras
description: You can read these utilities by following how each function constructs a list. Their type signatures show the inputs and results.

steps.description: alternate repeats the two-element list [a, b] n times and joins those lists with concat. Follow that definition when reading the example comment.
interleave returns the remaining list when either input is empty. With two nonempty inputs, it places one head from each before the recursive result.
everyNth pairs elements with indices starting at zero. Its local apply function transforms elements whose index is divisible by n.
euclidean starts with groups of True beats and False steps. It passes both groups and their counts to go.
The local go function returns concatenated groups in its base cases. Its guards choose how to combine groups and update the counts.
